The "Quality Standard" topic outlines the specific performance thresholds and regulatory benchmarks established for various clinical indicators within the ADHD diagnostic and treatment pathways. These standards are primarily set at a 90% compliance target for most indicators, ensuring high-quality care, systematic evaluation, and standardized monitoring for patients across the healthcare system.

For the diagnostic phase, [[Indikator 1]] requires that at least 90% of assessment processes include a somatic evaluation within 120 days of starting the ADHD assessment [^src1]. Similarly, [[Indikator 2b]] mandates a 90% standard for conducting manualized diagnostic interviews or environmental observations for patients aged 6–17 [^src1], a benchmark that is also reinforced as a regulatory standard by the [[ADHD-DATABASEN]] and [[indicator-2b]] frameworks [^src3]. The [[Styregruppen]] (Steering Group) has additionally set a 90% standard for the related indicator 2a [^src2]. Furthermore, [[Indikator 3]] requires that 90% of assessments involve a diagnostic conference with a specialist in child and adolescent psychiatry [^src1], a standard that is firmly established at 90% in later reporting [^src4].

In the treatment phase, quality standards focus heavily on coordination and education. [[Indikator 4]] sets a 90% threshold for holding coordinating network meetings during treatment [^src1], and [[Indikator 5]] requires that 90% of patients or their parents begin ADHD-related psychoeducation [^src1]. Both of these treatment indicators share a unified 90% standard in subsequent evaluations [^src5]. Notably, [[Indikator 6]] serves as an exception; it tracks the proportion of treatment courses where the patient is receiving ADHD medication, but it currently has no fixed quality standard set for this metric [^src1]. 

Overall, these quality standards form a comprehensive framework monitored by entities like the [[Styregruppen]] and the [[ADHD-DATABASEN]] to ensure that ADHD assessments and treatments adhere to rigorous, evidence-based clinical guidelines.

## Claims
- Indikator 1 har en standard på ≥ 90 % for andelen af udredningsforløb, hvor der er foretaget somatisk udredning senest 120 dage efter start af ADHD-udredning [^src1] (indikator-1)
  Type: quality-standard
  Page: 6
  Source: wikis/rkkp-adhd/raw/ADHD_2023.pdf, pages 6-10
- Indikator 2b har en standard på ≥ 90 % for andelen af udredningsforløb blandt 6–17 årige, hvor der er foretaget manualiseret diagnostisk interview eller miljøobservation [^src1] (indikator-2b)
  Type: quality-standard
  Page: 6
  Source: wikis/rkkp-adhd/raw/ADHD_2023.pdf, pages 6-10
- Indikator 3 har en standard på ≥ 90 % for andelen af udredningsforløb, hvor der er afholdt diagnostisk konference med speciallæge i børne- og ungdomspsykiatri [^src1] (indikator-3)
  Type: quality-standard
  Page: 6
  Source: wikis/rkkp-adhd/raw/ADHD_2023.pdf, pages 6-10
- Indikator 4 har en standard på ≥ 90 % for andelen af behandlingsforløb, hvor der er foretaget koordinerende netværksmøde [^src1] (indikator-4)
  Type: quality-standard
  Page: 6
  Source: wikis/rkkp-adhd/raw/ADHD_2023.pdf, pages 6-10
- Indikator 5 har en standard på ≥ 90 % for andelen af behandlingsforløb, hvor patienten/forældre har påbegyndt ADHD-relateret psykoedukation [^src1] (indikator-5)
  Type: quality-standard
  Page: 6
  Source: wikis/rkkp-adhd/raw/ADHD_2023.pdf, pages 6-10
- Indikator 6 har ingen fastsat standard for andelen af behandlingsforløb, hvor patienten er i behandling med ADHD-medicin [^src1] (indikator-6)
  Type: quality-standard
  Page: 6
  Source: wikis/rkkp-adhd/raw/ADHD_2023.pdf, pages 6-10
- Standarden for indikator 2a er ≥ 90 % [^src1] (styregruppen)
  Type: quality-standard
  Page: 11
  Source: wikis/rkkp-adhd/raw/ADHD_2023.pdf, pages 11-15
- Standarden for indikator 2b er ≥ 90 % [^src1] (adhd-databasen, indicator-2b)
  Type: regulatory-standard
  Page: 16
  Source: wikis/rkkp-adhd/raw/ADHD_2023.pdf, pages 16-20
- Standarden for Indikator 3 er fastlagt til 90 % [^src1] (indikator-3)
  Type: standard
  Page: 26
  Source: wikis/rkkp-adhd/raw/ADHD_2023.pdf, pages 26-30
